items.stem: Which task is an AI assistant most reliably good at?

options.text: Turning a long document you provide into a short summary.
Telling you the latest share price of a competitor.
Adding up a column of 200 invoice totals exactly.
Reporting what was said in a meeting it did not attend.

items.stem: An AI assistant gives you a specific, confident answer that turns out to be made up. What is this called?

options.text: A bias.
A hallucination.
A prompt.
A data breach.

items.stem: Which prompt is most likely to get a useful first draft?

options.text: Write something about the new expenses process.
Expenses email please, make it good.
You are an internal communications writer. Draft an email telling staff about the new expenses process, for people who submit claims monthly. Use five bullets.
Can you help with an email?

items.stem: In a prompt, what does the Format element describe?

options.text: Who the assistant should act as.
The background and constraints for the task.
The action you want the assistant to take.
The shape of the output, such as a table or a word limit.

items.stem: The assistant's first draft is too long and too formal. What is usually the quickest fix?

options.text: Give up and write it from scratch.
Reply asking for a friendlier version under 100 words.
Start a new chat with the same prompt.
Switch to a different AI tool.

items.stem: An AI summary includes a figure and a link to its source. What should you do before using the figure?

options.text: Nothing, because it gave a source.
Ask the assistant if it is sure.
Check that the link starts with https.
Open the source and find the figure yourself.

items.stem: Which details in an AI-drafted document most need checking against a source?

options.text: Names, numbers, quotes and links.
Headings and paragraph order.
Spelling and punctuation only.
The font and layout.

items.stem: Which of these is safe to paste into a free public AI tool your organisation has not approved?

options.text: A customer's complaint email, including their address.
Your team's unreleased budget figures.
A request for ideas for a team-building day.
The password for a shared reporting tool.

items.stem: You need help drafting a letter about a specific employee's situation. What is the safest approach?

options.text: Use the approved company assistant and describe the situation without names or identifying details.
Use any tool, then delete the chat afterwards.
Paste the employee's file so the draft is accurate.
Remove only the employee's surname.

items.stem: Which is the best first use of an AI assistant for a sales team?

options.text: Deciding which salesperson to let go.
Drafting routine follow-up emails after calls.
Interpreting a tricky contract clause for a client.
Setting the discount for the biggest account.

items.stem: You send a client an AI-drafted report that contains an error. Who is accountable?

options.text: The company that makes the AI tool.
The IT team that approved the tool.
No one, since AI errors are expected.
You, as the person who sent it.

items.stem: An AI draft would commit your company to a legal term you are unsure about. What should you do?

options.text: Send it, because the assistant is usually right.
Ask the assistant whether the term is legal.
Hold it and escalate to your manager or the legal team.
Send it and correct it later if needed.
